localizedValues.name: Elfin Lakes Shelter
localizedValues.description: The Elfin Shelter, which can accommodate 33 people on 22 bunks, is located next to the Elfin Lakes campground. Bunks are either single or double. The Elfin Shelter offers propane heating and cooking stoves. While your reservation guarantees you a spot, the beds are available on a first come, first served basis. Elfin shelter visitors should bring a sleeping bag and sleeping pad. Single people are asked to choose a single bunk to leave the doubles for couples. In some cases, you may be sharing a double bunk with other Elfin shelter visitors.

localizedValues.name: Other Access via Whistler Blackcomb Resort
Elfin Lakes
localizedValues.description: 11 km from the Diamond Head Parking Lot.  Suggested time 3.5 to 6 hours; one way.  Elevation change is approximately 700 meters.  The trail difficulty is moderate to strenuous. For current trail conditions please refer to the trail report on the Garibaldi Provincial Park website.  The campground has 35 sites, a day use shelter (for cooking), bear cache for food storage, and outhouses.  The campground offers splendid views and sits next to 2 small lakes near the north end of Paul Ridge. Mountain bikes are permitted on the trail from the Diamond Head parking lot to Elfin Lakes but not beyond.   Boil or treat your water.   Fires, domestic animals and motorized vehicles are not permitted in Garibaldi Park.

localizedValues.name: Garibaldi Lake
localizedValues.description: 9 km from the Black Tusk/Garibaldi Lake trailhead.  Suggested time 3 to 5 hours; one way.  Elevation change is approximately 900 meters.  Garibaldi Lake offers scenic views of the lake which is surrounded by stunning snow-capped peaks. The trail difficulty is moderate to strenuous. For current trail conditions please refer to the trail report on the Garibaldi Provincial Park website. Garibaldi Lake campground has 50 campsites, 4 outhouses and 4 day use shelters (for cooking and food storage).  Boil or treat your water.  Mountain bikes are not permitted on these trails.  Fires, domestic animals and motorized vehicles are not permitted in Garibaldi Park.

localizedValues.name: Taylor Meadows
localizedValues.description: 7.5 km from the Black Tusk/Garibaldi Lake trailhead.  Suggested time 3 to 5 hours; one way. Elevation change is approximately 950 meters. Taylor Meadows campground sits in a heather meadow with wildflowers and is closer to the Black Tusk and Panorama Ridge Trails. The trail difficulty is generally considered moderate or strenuous. For current trail conditions please refer to the trail report on the Garibaldi Provincial Park website. Taylor Meadows campground has 40 campsites, 3 outhouses and 2 day use shelters (for cooking and food storage).  Boil or treat your water.  Mountain bikes are not permitted on these trails. Fires, domestic animals and motorized vehicles are not permitted in Garibaldi Park.

localizedValues.name: Cheakamus Lake
localizedValues.description: Cheakamus Lake Campground is 3km from the parking lot and offers 10 cleared shoreline tent sites, pit toilet facilities and food hang facilities. Be aware food hang facilities exist but be prepared to hang your food as the facilities do fill up. Mountain bikes are permitted on these trails. Fires, domestic animals and motorized vehicles are not permitted in Garibaldi Park. The Cheakamus Lake area experiences increased black bear activity in the spring season. Please use caution while travelling through the area and respect their environment. Stay on the trail and never approach or feed the wildlife. Remember, “A fed bear is a dead bear”. Please check the BC Parks website for Bear Safety information.

localizedValues.name: Helm Creek
localizedValues.description: Helm Creek Campground is located 8.5 km from the Cheakamus Lake parking lot, and 18 km from the Garibaldi Lake parking lot. The elevation gain from Cheakamus Lake to the Campground is 600m. The Campground offers 30 tent platforms, pit toilet facilities and food hang facilities. Be aware food hang facilities exist but be prepared to hang your food as the facilities do fill up. Mountain biking is permitted on the Cheakamus Lake trail but may not be taken across the Cheakamus River bridge on the Helm Creek trail. Fires, domestic animals and motorized vehicles are not permitted in Garibaldi Park.

localizedValues.name: Rampart Ponds
localizedValues.description: Located 10 km north east of the Elfin Lakes shelter. Rampart Ponds Campground offers 12 tent platforms, pit toilet facilities and food storage facilities. While your reservation guarantees you a site, they are available on first come first serve basis. Please be bear smart and cook or store food away from camping areas.  Rampart ponds is 1.5km before Mamquam. There is no camping permitted at Mamquam Lake.  Fires, domestic animals or motorized vehicles are not allowed in Garibaldi Provincial Park. Campers are required to present a copy of their reservation details when requested by a Park Ranger. Winter travel to Rampart Ponds is not recommended due to multiple avalanche paths and complex avalanche terrain.

localizedValues.name: Russet Lake
localizedValues.description: Russet Lake is located 14.5 km from Whistler village via the Singing Pass trail and 12.5 km from the top of the Whistler gondola. The elevation gain from the village is 1400 meters. The trail difficulty is moderate to strenuous. For current trail conditions please refer to the trail report on the Garibaldi Provincial Park website.  The Russet Lake Campground offers 7 dirt sites and one pit toilet. Please use the Russet Lake Hut for food storage.  The Russet Lake Hut offers 2 tables and 2 benches. Services are limited and there are no garbage facilities, please Pack Out what you Packed In. Boil or treat your water.  Fires, domestic animals and motorized vehicles are not permitted in Garibaldi Park. Mountain bikes are not permitted on these trails.

localizedValues.name: Singing Creek
localizedValues.description: Singing Creek Campground is located 7 km from the parking lot with 50m of elevation gain. It offers 6 cleared tent sites, pit toilet facilities and food hang facilities. Be aware food storage facilities exist but be prepared to hang your food as the facilities do fill up. Mountain bikes are permitted on these trails. Fires, domestic animals, and motorized vehicles are not permitted in Garibaldi Park. The Cheakamus Lake area experiences increased black bear activity in the spring season. Please use caution while travelling through the area and respect their environment. Stay on the trail and never approach or feed the wildlife. Remember, “A fed bear is a dead bear.” Please check the BC Parks website for Bear Safety information.

localizedValues.name: Wedgemount
localizedValues.description: Wedgemount Lake Campground is located 7 km from the Wedgemount trailhead. The elevation gain is approximately  1100m. The trail difficulty is strenuous to difficult. For current trail conditions please refer to the trail report on the Garibaldi Provincial Park website.  The Wedgemount Campground offers 20 tent sites. 10 of those sites are next to the Wedge hut and the permanent pit toilet, the other 10 sites are located on the lake shore about 500 meters away from the hut location. The lake side location offers a seasonal pit toilet from July 1st to September 15th. Please use the hut for food storage.  Services are limited and there are no garbage facilities, please Pack Out what you Packed In. Boil or treat your water.  Fires, domestic animals and motorized vehicles are not permitted in Garibaldi Park. Mountain bikes are not permitted on these trails.

localizedValues.name: Red Heather
localizedValues.description: Located 5 km on the Diamondhead access trail to Elfin Lakes, the Red Heather area offers a day use shelter equipped with 2 picnic tables, a propane hot plate, a wash sink, a cooking counter, a wood stove (winter use only) and pit toilet facilities. Please keep woodstove fires small to ensure that wood supplies last through the winter season. Camping is not permitted in the shelter. There are 15 on snow campsites available for reservation in the winter season only. Campers are required to present a copy of their reservation details when requested by a Park Ranger.

localizedValues.name: Wilderness Camping Area
localizedValues.description:
Wilderness Camping is not reservable online. Contact the call centre at 1-800-689-9025 (1-519-858-6161 internationally) to make a reservation. For further details, please visit Garibaldi Park Wilderness Camping Area.

Wilderness camping reservations are available to mountaineers, climbers, ski tourers, and others with advanced skills in wilderness travel.

Wilderness camping is only permitted in the Wilderness Camping Area [PDF]. You may be evicted or fined for using a wilderness camping reservation to camp anywhere else in the park.

No facilities are provided in the wilderness area. Wilderness campers must follow Leave No Trace outdoor ethics. Please be bear smart and cook and store food away from camping areas.

Wilderness campers must be experienced with advanced trip planning and know and carry appropriate gear for intended activities. Winter travelers must understand avalanche forecasts, and have proper avalanche training and gear.

Fires, domestic animals, or motorized vehicles are not allowed in Garibaldi Provincial Park.

Wilderness campers must present a copy of their reservation details when requested by a Park Ranger.
